thread:
Alex C: Hey team — quick validation bounce for Tidecrest private deploy. Customer finished VPC peering yesterday, we need to confirm KMS log streaming + network egress rules before cutover. Any immediate blockers?
Sam N: I pulled their VPC peering config. Looks ok but public egress is via NAT in us-west-2a only. We should confirm multi-AZ egress or they'll have asymmetric flows.
Mira S: KMS side: they want customer-managed keys (CMEK). We need a KMS key policy template and a brief on how we expect grants for the inference nodes. Also confirm CloudTrail -> S3 bucket encryption + lifecycle for audit logs.
Jordan P: Copy. Alex, do we have their role ARNs for the inference instances? I can draft the minimal IAM trust policy once I have that.
Alex C: They shared a list in the onboarding doc — added to the shared folder: https://redwood.example/s/tidecrest/onboard (private). Roles are: arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/tidecrest-infer, arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/tidecrest-admin
Sam N: Networking quick checklist: 1) Allow outbound 443 to kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com 2) Allow outbound 443 to s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com (for audit delivery) 3) Ensure route tables for private subnets point to NAT in each AZ or to a centralized proxy.
Mira S: KMS specifics: add a statement in key policy allowing sts:AssumeRole from arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/tidecrest-infer and allow kms:GenerateDataKey* for the inference role. Also recommend an OrganizationBinding condition if they're using org accounts.
Jordan P: For end-to-end test, I'll run a validation script that does: 
```
curl -v https://kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ --resolve kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com:443:<NAT_IP>\naws s3 ls s3://tidecrest-logs --region us-west-2
```
Sam N: Note: if they have strict egress IPs, we need their NAT IPs for the allowlist. Ask ops to confirm if EIPs are assigned.
Alex C: @Sam N @Mira S I've asked Tidecrest to provide EIPs + list of service accounts by EOD. Also asked them to confirm whether they want logs shipped to Splunk or retained in S3 only.
infra-bot: Ticket #CS-4927 created for "Tidecrest private deploy: KMS + network validation" — assignee: Jordan P. https://redwood.example/tickets/CS-4927
Mira S: If they pick Splunk, we need the HEC endpoint + token and ensure the S3-to-Splunk lambda has kms:Decrypt on the rotation key.
Jordan P: I'll take CS-4927. Plan: run network egress checks, validate assume-role flow against KMS, simulate a log write to S3, and confirm CloudTrail delivery. ETA tomorrow morning.
Alex C: Perfect — low risk but callout for asymmetric NAT. If ops can't provide EIPs per AZ, we might suggest a small HA proxy so we don't rely on single-AZ NAT.
Sam N: Agreed. I'll flag infra to avoid single NAT. :thumbsup:
Mira S: Also adding a note to the key policy template about rotation schedule and who in their team can manage key rotation (minimize admins).
Alex C: Great. I'll follow up with Tidecrest and update the shared doc. Thanks all. :wave:
